named_beneficiary.source: Hebrew Wikisource, consolidated Basic Law: The Judiciary, ss. 4, 4A, 4B; Knesset OData KNS_Bill(2201200).SummaryLaw
named_beneficiary.support: Committee composition stated in general terms: two MKs, "one from the coalition factions ... and one from the opposition factions"; amended provisions apply "from the start of the 26th Knesset's term".
named_beneficiary.note: The text names no officeholder or sitting government; it applies to whichever coalition and opposition exist from the next Knesset onward. Explanatory notes to the 2023 first-reading bill were not fetched (fs.knesset.gov.il bot check). The Knesset summary shows no specific beneficiary.

immediate_effect.source: Hebrew Wikisource consolidated Basic Law: The Judiciary, notes on ss. 4(b), 4(d), 4(e), 4(f), 4A, 4B
immediate_effect.support: Each amended provision carries the note "(החל מיום תחילת כהונתה של הכנסת העשרים ושש)" ('from the day the 26th Knesset's term begins').
immediate_effect.note: Basis: stated, effect after the next general election. Published 1 April 2025 (KNS_Bill PublicationDate; Sefer HaHukim 3388, p. 434). The note is Wikisource's rendering of the amending law's commencement provision; the gazette PDF was not read.

coalition_only.support: Vote 43884, 27 Mar 2025 07:36: 67 for, 1 against (Miki Levy), 2 present and not voting (Walid Alhwashla, Merav Michaeli).
coalition_only.note: Against: Miki Levy (Yesh Atid). Present and not voting: Walid Alhwashla (Ra'am), Merav Michaeli (Labor). No opposition member voted for. The four HaYamin HaMamlachti members who voted for (Gideon Sa'ar, Ze'ev Elkin, Sharren Haskel, Michel Buskila) belonged to the coalition on the day: KNS_PersonToPosition lists Sa'ar as Foreign Minister from 8 Nov 2024, Elkin as additional minister in the Finance Ministry from 8 Nov 2024, and Haskel as deputy foreign minister from 11 Nov 2024. Otzma Yehudit had rejoined the government (Ben Gvir Minister of National Security again from 19 Mar 2025). UTJ held deputy-minister posts until July 2025. The OData result rows carry no faction field, so the faction tallies come from the vote record supplied.

expedited.support: First reading: vote 38298, 2023-02-20. Third reading: vote 43884, 2025-03-27. 766 days apart.
expedited.note: Vote 38298 was on the same bill ID 2201200 under its earlier title, "הצעת חוק-יסוד: השפיטה (תיקון מס' 3) (חיזוק הפרדת הרשויות)". The bill is a committee bill (SubTypeDesc 'ועדה'); its second/third-reading version is dated 15 Jan 2025 in KNS_DocumentBill. No OData record shows a special procedure shortening the committee stage; committee session records were not searched.

scope.source: Hebrew Wikisource consolidated Basic Law: The Judiciary, ss. 4(b)-(f), 4A, 4B
scope.support: Supreme Court selection "by a majority of five members including one listed in 4(d)(2) and one listed in 4(d)(3)" (coalition and opposition).
scope.note: The amendment removes the Bar Association's two seats and replaces them with two public representatives, one elected by coalition MKs and one by opposition MKs; for Supreme Court appointments a sitting judge's vote is no longer part of the required majority. It does not remove a check outright: it substitutes an alternative under which the opposition's consent is required. The three judges keep their seats and remain required for lower-court appointments. Section 4A lets coalition and opposition each break a deadlock once per Knesset; s.4B bars appointments during election periods or after the government resigns. The replaced 7-of-9 rule sits in the Courts Law and was not checked.

temporary_provision.source: Hebrew Wikisource consolidated Basic Law: The Judiciary; KNS_Bill(2201200)
temporary_provision.support: Permanent amendment to ss. 4, 4A, 4B; no 'הוראת שעה' designation.
temporary_provision.note: Section 4A's deadlock mechanism may be used once per Knesset term: a recurring rule, not a single instance.

targets_judiciary.support: "בהרכב הוועדה לבחירת שופטים, במקום שני נציגי לשכת עורכי הדין, יבחרו סיעות הקואליציה וסיעות האופוזיציה ... שני נציגי ציבור"
targets_judiciary.note: Subject: judicial appointments, the Committee's composition and voting rules.

deviation_tier.source: Hebrew Wikisource consolidated Basic Law: The Judiciary, ss. 4(b)(1), 4(e), 4A, 4B
deviation_tier.support: s.4(e): Supreme Court selection needs five votes including a coalition and an opposition member, with no judge required.
deviation_tier.note: Values engaged: an independent judiciary (principal) and the separation of powers. Politically chosen members rise from four of nine to six of nine, and judges lose their required vote on Supreme Court appointments. Limited, not sharp: judges keep three seats, opposition consent is required, effect is deferred to the 26th Knesset, and s.4B adds a safeguard around elections. Under contradiction-takes-precedence, the entrenching elements do not change the tier.

direction.source: Hebrew Wikisource consolidated Basic Law: The Judiciary, ss. 4(b)(1), 4(e), 4A
direction.support: Bar Association seats replaced by representatives "שייבחרו בכנסת" (elected in the Knesset); judges' vote not required for Supreme Court selection.
direction.note: Principal axis: judicial independence, through the appointments process; Illiberal because political bodies gain a larger say over appointments. Liberal-leaning elements (the guaranteed opposition role, the s.4B freeze) are secondary. Jewish identity, minority rights and women's rights are not engaged.

deviations: The Wikisource consolidated page for Basic Law: The Judiciary carries editorial references to a High Court judgment on Amendment No. 3 (a different enactment); not opened, nothing used.

The amending law's own text was not reached: Wikisource has no separate page for Amendment No. 4 (404), and the gazette PDF and explanatory notes on fs.knesset.gov.il were not tried because of the bot check. Commencement rests on Wikisource's notes.
The Wikisource search API rate-limited once; a later fetch with a descriptive User-Agent worked.
